name: Boil water
summary: The one method that reliably kills every pathogen — bring it to a rolling boil.
time: as long as the fire takes, plus a minute at the boil

steps.text: Let cloudy water settle, then pour off the clear top, or strain it through cloth.
steps.why: Sediment does not stop the boil working, but it carries taste and it fouls a container.

steps.text: Bring the water to a ROLLING boil — a full, tumbling, continuous boil, not the first bubbles.
Hold the rolling boil for one minute. Above roughly 2,000 m of altitude, hold it for three.
Cover and let it cool in the same container you boiled it in.
steps.why: Pouring hot clean water into a dirty vessel recontaminates every bit of it.

verify: A rolling boil is a visual check you cannot fake — the surface tumbles continuously.
If you have no container that can take direct heat, drop fire-heated rocks into a bark, hide or wooden vessel until the water boils; rocks from a riverbed can burst, so use dry rocks.
limits: Boiling kills bacteria, viruses, protozoa and their cysts. It removes NOTHING dissolved — no salt, no heavy metals, no pesticides, no chemical runoff, and no toxin from a cyanobacteria bloom. It concentrates them, because water leaves as steam and the contaminant stays.
Water from a mine tailing, an industrial site, a road ditch, or a pond with a blue-green surface scum is not made drinkable by boiling.
cautions: Getting to a boil is the safe way to think about it — the pasteurization temperature is lower, but you cannot measure temperature and you can see a boil.
